gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: The festival went ahead ___ the fact that both headliners had cancelled.
gaps.hint: not a cause but a concession
gaps.explanation: The festival happened in spite of the cancellations: despite, not because of.

gaps.sentence: ___ a slight delay in Rome, the whole journey went smoothly.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from' sets the delay aside as the only problem.

gaps.sentence: I'll tell you everything ___ you promise to keep it between us.
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' sets the condition attached to the promise.

gaps.sentence: British houses usually have gardens, ___ flats in Spain often have balconies.
We'd have held the wedding in the garden ___ it had poured with rain.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if + past perfect' concedes a hypothetical condition in the past.
